metadata.title: Morgan Stanley Resets Okta Stock Price Target For Rest of Year

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Okta (NASDAQ:OKTA) picked up a fresh bullish call qfrom Morgan Stanley after the cybersecurity company's recent investor event strengthened the bank's conviction in its exposure to securing AI agents.
Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) analyst Meta (NASDAQ:META) Marshall raised her price target on Okta to $245 from $200 while reiterating an Overweight rating.
The stock has already surged roughly 140% in 2026, but Marshall still sees room for additional gains as enterprises confront a new cybersecurity challenge: managing the identities and permissions of autonomous AI agents.
For Okta, the name is generally seen as a secular winner from Agentic Identity exposure, Marshall said.
The investment case is also benefiting from stretched valuations across cybersecurity leaders such as Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike.
Marshall said investors appear increasingly willing to consider a broader group of cybersecurity stocks as valuations on some established winners rise.
Okta used its September 23 Oktane event to highlight new AI-agent identity products and partnerships, reinforcing its push into a market that could become increasingly important as companies deploy more autonomous software.
Still, the event did not deliver everything investors wanted.
Some analysts were disappointed that Okta provided no new financial guidance or updated longer-term targets, leaving the near-term earnings picture largely unchanged.
Marshall also cautioned that the opportunity will likely develop gradually.
We continue to think this will come on slowly, with moves this year related to technical debt being addressed, but continue to see runway with the name, she said.
Investor Takeaway
Morgan Stanley's higher target suggests the Okta story is increasingly shifting from traditional workforce identity toward securing the next generation of AI-driven enterprise applications.
That could expand Okta's addressable market as businesses need tighter controls over what AI agents can access and execute.
But after a 140% rally, expectations are already much higher.
Investors should watch whether agentic-identity products begin translating into stronger bookings, larger customer deployments and faster revenue growth.
If that happens, Okta could justify a higher valuation. If adoption remains slow, the stock's sharp 2026 run leaves less room for execution mistakes.
